strings.d1.s0.name: MASP
strings.d1.s0.tips: Lina Bo Bardi's museum suspended in mid-air; Van Gogh and Portinari on glass easels. Free on Tuesdays, and Paulista is car-free on Sundays.
strings.d1.s1.name: Avenida Paulista
strings.d1.s1.tips: The financial boulevard; pedestrian-only on Sundays, with street musicians and Japan House.
strings.d1.s2.name: Bráz Pizzaria Paulista
strings.d1.s2.tips: São Paulo pizza (the city ranks as the world's second pizza city); thin crust, muçarela de búfala (buffalo mozzarella).
strings.d1.s3.name: Parque Trianon
strings.d1.s3.tips: A remnant of Atlantic forest on Paulista; welcome shade.
strings.d1.s4.name: Sesc Avenida Paulista Terası
strings.d1.s4.tips: A free rooftop terrace with a city panorama, inside a cultural centre.
strings.d1.b0.name: Mocotó Vila Medeiros
strings.d1.b0.tips: A legend of northeastern Brazilian cooking; far out but worth it (take an Uber).
strings.d1.b1.name: Instituto Moreira Salles
strings.d1.b1.tips: Photography museum with a terrace, on Paulista; free.
strings.d2.s0.name: Mercado Municipal Mercadão
strings.d2.s0.tips: A 1933 market with stained-glass windows; try the mortadella sandwich (Hocca Bar, 300 g) and pastel de bacalhau (salt cod pastry), and taste exotic fruit (the vendors are insistent).
strings.d2.s1.name: Catedral da Sé & Marco Zero
strings.d2.s1.tips: A neo-Gothic cathedral and the city's zero point; nearby is Pátio do Colégio (founded in 1554).
strings.d2.s2.name: Edifício Martinelli / Farol Santander
strings.d2.s2.tips: A 1929 skyscraper; Farol Santander has a viewing deck on the 26th floor and a skate ramp.
strings.d2.s3.name: Theatro Municipal
strings.d2.s3.tips: A copy of the Paris Opera; tours run Wednesday to Friday, on Praça Ramos de Azevedo.
strings.d2.s4.name: Edifício Copan
strings.d2.s4.tips: Niemeyer's wavy building with 1,160 apartments; see it from outside (the terrace may be closed), and try Bar da Dona Onça.
strings.d2.b0.name: Bar da Dona Onça Copan
strings.d2.b0.tips: Brazilian classics at the foot of the Copan; feijoada (black bean and pork stew) on Saturdays.
strings.d2.b1.name: Pinacoteca do Estado
strings.d2.b1.tips: A museum in a Ramos de Azevedo brick building; Brazilian art, free on Saturdays, next to Luz station.
strings.d3.s0.name: Parque Ibirapuera
strings.d3.s0.tips: The city's Central Park, with Niemeyer pavilions; bikes, a lake and the Oca.
strings.d3.s1.name: Museu Afro Brasil
strings.d3.s1.tips: African-Brazilian culture inside the park; slavery and art.
strings.d3.s2.name: Figueira Rubaiyat Jardins
strings.d3.s2.tips: Steak under a giant fig tree, in the upscale Jardins district.
strings.d3.s3.name: Rua Oscar Freire
strings.d3.s3.tips: Brazil's most luxurious street; the Havaianas flagship store and Melissa.
strings.d3.s4.name: Museu da Imagem e do Som
strings.d3.s4.tips: Museum of sound and image; pop exhibitions.
strings.d3.b0.name: A Casa do Porco
strings.d3.b0.tips: Among the world's 50 best restaurants; pork tasting menu, in the Centre. Book months ahead.
strings.d3.b1.name: Casa de Vidro Lina Bo Bardi
strings.d3.b1.tips: The architect's glass house in Morumbi; reservation required.
strings.d4.s0.name: Beco do Batman
strings.d4.s0.tips: Graffiti on Batman Alley in Vila Madalena; it changes every week.
strings.d4.s1.name: Coffee Lab Vila Madalena
strings.d4.s1.tips: A Brazilian coffee laboratory; run by Isabela Raposeiras.
strings.d4.s2.name: Mercado de Pinheiros
strings.d4.s2.tips: A neighbourhood market; Comedoria Gonzales serves Peruvian food by Rodrigo Oliveira.
strings.d4.s3.name: Instituto Tomie Ohtake
strings.d4.s3.tips: Ruy Ohtake's purple-and-red building in Pinheiros; free exhibitions.
strings.d4.s4.name: Vila Madalena Bar Akşamı São Cristóvão
strings.d4.s4.tips: A football-fanatic bar on Rua Aspicuelta; street party on Fridays and Saturdays.
strings.d4.b0.name: Praça Benedito Calixto Pazarı
strings.d4.b0.tips: Saturday antiques and crafts market; choro music.
strings.d4.b1.name: Bar Veloso Vila Mariana
strings.d4.b1.tips: The city's best coxinha (chicken croquette) and caipirinha; expect a queue.
strings.d5.s0.name: Liberdade Japon Mahallesi
strings.d5.s0.tips: The largest Japanese community outside Japan; red torii gates and lanterns, plus the Praça da Liberdade market on Sundays.
strings.d5.s1.name: Liberdade Ramen Aska
strings.d5.s1.tips: A small Japanese ramen shop; queue, cash only.
strings.d5.s2.name: Museu da Imigração Mooca
strings.d5.s2.tips: A former immigrant hostel (like Ellis Island); Italian, Japanese and Turkish-Syrian migration.
strings.d5.s3.name: Bixiga Italyan Mahallesi
strings.d5.s3.tips: Cantinas on Rua 13 de Maio; the Vai-Vai samba school, and the Nossa Senhora Achiropita festival in August.
strings.d5.s4.name: Cantina Famiglia Mancini
strings.d5.s4.tips: A cantina on Rua Avanhandava dating from 1980; giant portions of pasta, and a queue.
strings.d5.b0.name: Templo Busshinji Liberdade
strings.d5.b0.tips: A Zen temple; an alternative to the museum.
strings.d5.b1.name: Sujinho Consolação
strings.d5.b1.tips: A late-night steakhouse; churrasco (grilled meat), open 24 hours.
strings.d6.s0.name: Embu das Artes Feira de Artesanato
strings.d6.s0.tips: A colonial artists' town 27 km away; crafts fair at weekends (shops only on weekdays), one hour by bus.
strings.d6.s1.name: Igreja Nossa Senhora do Rosário Embu
strings.d6.s1.tips: A 1690 Jesuit church with a museum of sacred art.
strings.d6.s2.name: Restaurante Os Girassóis Embu
strings.d6.s2.tips: A restaurant in a colonial house; feijoada and Minas Gerais cooking.
strings.d6.s3.name: Embu Antikacılar & Rüstik Mobilya
strings.d6.s3.tips: Wooden furniture and ceramics; shipping available.
strings.d6.s4.name: Parque Villa-Lobos Dönüş
strings.d6.s4.tips: A park in western São Paulo; sunset and cycling.
strings.d6.b0.name: Parque Estadual da Cantareira
strings.d6.b0.tips: Atlantic forest north of the city; Pedra Grande viewpoint, nature instead of Embu.
strings.d6.b1.name: Casa do Sino Embu
strings.d7.s0.name: Parque Buenos Aires Higienópolis
strings.d7.s0.tips: A French-style garden; a neighbourhood morning.
strings.d7.s1.name: Padaria Santa Teresa
strings.d7.s1.tips: Breakfast at a padaria (Brazilian bakery); pão na chapa (grilled buttered bread) and pingado (coffee with milk), a farewell treat.
strings.d7.s2.name: Museu do Futebol Pacaembu
strings.d7.s2.tips: A football museum inside Pacaembu stadium; Pelé and Garrincha, interactive.
strings.d7.s3.name: Guarulhos Havalimanı Uber
strings.d7.s3.tips: 45-90 minutes by Uber depending on traffic; farewell.
strings.d7.b0.name: Rua Augusta Kahve Bar
strings.d7.b1.name: Museu do Ipiranga
strings.d7.b1.tips: The Independence Museum, restored in 2022; gardens, an alternative to football.
strings.note0: The metro is safe and clean (Bilhete Único card); Uber and 99 are cheap; traffic is terrible (17:00-20:00). Guarulhos is 45-90 minutes away; Congonhas is inside the city.
strings.note1: June to September is the dry winter, 15-24°C (the most comfortable, cool at night); the Bixiga festival is in August; fog is possible.
strings.note2: SAFETY: in the Centre (Sé, Luz, 25 de Março) keep your wallet in front by day and avoid it when empty at night; don't take your phone out on the street. Paulista, Jardins and Vila Madalena are relaxed.
strings.note3: Pizza 80-100 BRL, per-kilo restaurant 50, mortadella sandwich 40, padaria breakfast 30; 10% service is included; Pix and cards are accepted everywhere.
strings.note4: MASP is free on Tuesdays and Pinacoteca on Saturdays; Paulista is pedestrian-only on Sundays; book A Casa do Porco months ahead; Embu is best at weekends.
strings.note5: Coxinha, pão de queijo (cheese bread), pastel, mortadella, feijoada (Wednesday and Saturday), caipirinha; Japanese food in Liberdade.
